scenes.title: Introduction — five-step Read Aloud formula
scenes.narration: P T E Academic Read Aloud. Stop reading word by word. This lesson introduces a five-step formula: preview, chunk, stress, connect, and finish. Use these techniques together to build more natural fluency, clearer pronunciation, and better reading rhythm.

scenes.title: Step 1 — Preview difficult words
scenes.narration: Step one: preview. Before you begin speaking, identify difficult words in the sentence. Here, focus on bioluminescence, organisms, and illumination. Prepare their pronunciation in advance. The goal is to avoid hesitation when reading the full sentence aloud.

scenes.title: Step 2 — Chunk into phrases
scenes.narration: Step two: chunk. Divide the scientific sentence into meaningful phrases. Follow the coloured highlights to see where each phrase begins and ends. Read each group smoothly, then pause briefly at a natural boundary. Don't stop after every individual word.

scenes.title: Step 3 — Stress content words
scenes.narration: Step three: stress. Emphasise the words that carry the main meaning, rather than giving every word equal weight. Notice the highlighted content words, including phenomenon, bioluminescence, organisms, produce light, chemical reactions, and illumination. Keep the smaller linking words lighter.

scenes.title: Step 4 — Connect naturally
scenes.narration: Step four: connect. Link words naturally within each phrase so your reading flows. The blue markings show words that belong together. Maintain smooth transitions between them and use a short pause only where it helps the meaning. Avoid robotic, word-by-word delivery.

scenes.title: Step 5 — Finish clearly
scenes.narration: Step five: finish. Keep a steady pace through the final phrase. Don't rush, trail off, or drop the last words. The slide shows how to complete external source of illumination clearly. End with control and a natural cadence.

scenes.title: Five scientific sentences for practice
scenes.narration: Finally, practise the method with these five scientific sentences. They include challenging vocabulary from bioluminescence, nanotechnology, photosynthesis, neuroplasticity, and thermodynamics. For each sentence, preview unfamiliar words, find useful chunks, stress key terms, connect naturally, and finish clearly. Save this exercise for repeated practice.
